resources.string: %1$d dictionaries · indexing %2$d in the background… · AI: %3$s
AI is off: choose a provider in InkPeek settings → AI.
Preparing: %1$s (first use, try again in a minute)
No key: type it below or put it into %1$s
No network: AI tabs work online; dictionaries work offline.
Word by word (works offline; › opens a word):
No network. AI needs the internet; the Dictionary tab works offline.
The AI server does not answer. Check the internet connection or VPN.
The AI service refused the request. Check the network or VPN and the API key.
The API key was rejected: check it in InkPeek settings.
Too many requests: the provider\'s limit. Try again in a minute.
No credits left on this key.
No API key: add one in InkPeek settings or in /sdcard/InkPeek/keys/.
No model chosen: pick one in InkPeek settings → AI.
The AI request failed. Try again; if it repeats, check the AI settings.
Not needed for a home server; cloud services need one.
The server does not answer: %1$s\nCheck the address and that the server is running.
Nothing saved yet: tap ☆ in the card.
The grammar of the form or phrase and its rule; harder words or synonyms.
What it means here, register, nuances; three examples with a translation.
Packs and other dictionaries; a phrase: word by word. Works offline.
Keeps it in Notes; a filled star: it is there already.
Your saved words and phrases and the history, also in the settings.
Offline translation on the device first, AI translation next to it (asked when you tap it).
Offline translation needs a language pack: InkPeek settings → Languages.
The list of language packs is not available yet (%1$s).
This looks like %1$s: InkPeek has no language pack for it yet.
No dictionaries yet: InkPeek settings → Languages (packs or other dictionaries).
No network: the list of language packs needs the internet.
Closes the card; Back does the same. Held: opens InkPeek (its search field, the settings).
By content: a small card that grows with its text, up to 80%.
The card\'s share of the screen width.
\"Where the reading app asks\" keeps the selected word visible (Librera, FBReader).
The card\'s text; the header is a little larger.
Off: only the open page; Back or a tap outside closes the card.
What you open is kept in Notes → History, with how many times you looked it up. Off: nothing is written; what is there stays until you clear it.
Light, dark (white on black) or as Android\'s night mode: the card and the settings.
Articles in the Dictionary tab and the word-by-word translation.
The card\'s header: article, plural, verb forms (das Haus, pl. Häuser).
None yet: download some or import files (StarDict, as in KOReader).
Short translations, part of speech and gender; forms lead to the base (ging → gehen).
Full Wiktionary articles: pronunciation, all senses, examples.
Older compact dictionaries without word forms; WikDict is usually better.
★ — recommended: compact translations into the app\'s language.
Off: everything works offline. Its tabs in the card: AI → Modules.
Offline translation needs the InkPeek pack \"%1$s → %2$s\": InkPeek settings → Languages.
None yet: choose pairs under Download packs… below.
Remove the pack \"%1$s\"? It can be downloaded again.
Dictionary, grammar and translation for a pair of languages; built and tested by the project on GitHub.
Tap a pair to download it: dictionary, grammar and offline translation.
Dictionary, grammar and offline translation: %1$d MB to download.
Dictionaries are read from here; downloads and imports go here.
Delete \"%1$s\"? Its files are deleted from %2$s.

Wiktionary articles in the answer language (via kaikki.org); English words also from the translation tables of the English Wiktionary; WikDict where Wiktionary has no article. The first line: the word with its grammar and the main meanings.
Gender, plural, verb forms, irregular or strong — from Wiktionary\'s inflection tables. Every form leads to its word: Häusern → Haus, went → go. Only what Wiktionary says, no guessing.
fastText (lid.176); when it is unsure (a word or two), the dictionary that knows more of the words decides.
Our scripts on GitHub build every pack from these open sources and check it with tests (words and their forms) before publishing; the app downloads only from the project\'s releases.

Any StarDict dictionary, the format KOReader, GoldenDict and ColorDict use: download one from WikDict, Wiktionary or FreeDict, import files, or point the app to a folder. In the card they come after the packs by default (Card → Article → Dictionary order); each line is signed with its name.

Pick the dictionary\'s files together (.ifo, .idx or .idx.gz, .dict or .dict.dz, .syn if there is one) or one archive: zip, tar, tar.gz, tar.bz2, tar.xz, tar.zst. Every dictionary in it gets its own folder.
Other dictionaries are read from one folder, and downloads and imports go into it. Choose KOReader\'s (koreader/data/dict) and both apps share the same dictionaries; deleting one deletes it for both.
From the provider\'s list; free ones are marked.
An OpenAI-compatible server; for a home one change only the IP.
Each part is one key of the answer: its name stays, what to write there can change.
Answer language, brevity, formatting: for every request.
{lang} is the answer language. This text goes with every AI request.
Optional tabs on top of the offline core: AI translation, Analysis and Context. Dictionary, grammar and offline translation never need it; with AI off its tabs are gone.
A word: its base form, gender, forms and main meanings; a phrase or passage: a natural translation that keeps the sentence type. Without a network Translate shows the offline translation.
Type the key here or put it into a file in InkPeek/keys (anthropic.key, openai.key, openrouter.key). The key never goes to logs, the screen or exports.
LM Studio, Ollama, llama.cpp, vLLM and other servers with the OpenAI API: choose a preset and change the IP. No cloud, no key; the answer may take longer.
OpenRouter has free models: open the model list and turn on Free only. Free models are slower and change often.
From an article to the list or to word by word; after Look up, to the word before.
Grammar: which form it is, how it is built and the rule behind it. Words: the harder words, or synonyms and related ones.
Explanation: what it means here, register, idioms, nuances. Examples: three everyday sentences with a translation.
Import takes StarDict files (.ifo with its .idx and .dict or .dict.dz, picked together) or an archive with them.
A pop-up dictionary and translator for e-book readers: language packs, your own StarDict dictionaries, offline translation; AI if you want it.
github.com/kafeg/inkpeek · MIT · packs: CC BY-SA, MPL
Short lines, a tap for the article; or full articles, ◀ ▶ between dictionaries.
Packs and other dictionaries in one list.
The card shows them top to bottom. Switched-off ones are not here.
Not a font InkPeek can read: %1$s
None yet: fonts from fonts/, koreader/fonts, or choose a file.
Android\'s fonts that have every letter the card needs: ä ß é ł д ж.
From fonts/, koreader/fonts and InkPeek/fonts; ✕ deletes a chosen file.
Off by default: e-ink shows a dim as a grey layer over the page.
This device: %1$s GB of memory; int8 acceleration: %2$s.
Through English: the meaning comes through; du/Sie, gender and idioms get lost. Works everywhere.
Straight from language to language, no English: more accurate, knows idioms. Helsinki models, ~170 MB each; needs 4 GB of memory.
Tencent\'s AI on the device, straight between languages: 1.1 GB; needs 6 GB of memory and int8 acceleration.
No model for %1$s: Mozilla translates them.
Needs %1$s GB of memory; this device has %2$s GB.
Needs a processor with int8 acceleration (dot product).
≈ %1$s s per phrase on this device
Not in the packs list yet.
Same root: prefixed verbs (anmachen, zumachen), phrasal verbs (make up), derived words.
Synonyms and antonyms, the frequent ones first.
Set phrases and idioms with the word, from the dictionary.
The table of forms and the IPA.
The form and how it is built; for a phrase, its constructions and the rule.
Harder words of a phrase; for a word, its synonyms and related words.
Words of the same root: prefixed verbs, phrasal verbs, derived words.
How the close words differ, opposites marked ≠.
What it means here, register, nuances.
Three everyday sentences with their translation.
Set phrases and idioms with the word and their meaning.
Where the word comes from, with a link to remember it.
Everything at once — saved words and phrases, the history and the AI answers — to a file in Download/InkPeek, and back: an import adds what this device does not have.
A TSV list for Anki or a spreadsheet: text, meaning, AI translation, language, date. It cannot be imported back — to move notes to another device, use Export below.
This is not an InkPeek backup: Import takes the inkpeek-backup-….db file that Export makes. A .tsv list is for Anki or a spreadsheet.
Dictionaries, translations and AI answers come in this language; the packs into it come first.
Remove this model (%1$d MB)? Its method uses Mozilla for these pairs until it is downloaded again.
An AI choice asks AI on every opening.
No offline translation: the Translate tab is AI only.
FBReader: Settings → Dictionary and translator: “Look up single word in” and “Translate phrases via” → ColorDict 3.

KOReader: it calls only the dictionary apps it knows. The button below adds InkPeek to koreader/dictionaries.lua (its other entries stay); then Settings → Dictionary settings → Use external dictionary → InkPeek.
InkPeek is added to KOReader: restart it and choose InkPeek
Librera, AlReaderX, Cool Reader, Moon+: their dictionary setting → ColorDict or GoldenDict. Any app: the text selection menu → Look up in InkPeek, or Share → InkPeek.
Each pair has a label: full — the dictionary knows 85 % or more of the 5,000 most frequent words, and offline translation is there; basic — 60 % or more; experimental — less.
For the dictionaries\' folders and InkPeek\'s own on shared storage.
Ask the other AI tabs at once
Opening one asks for the others too: they open without waiting.
Double tap or hold a word to select it; drag the handles to select more.
Triple tap selects the paragraph (not in the card\'s header: there a double tap often comes as three).
A row\'s text is selected the same way; the › arrow on its right opens it.
Opens on what Card → Opening says: offline translation, AI translation, word by word, Analysis or Context. No translation for the text → Dictionary.

The word\'s base form with its article, plural and forms; under it the form you selected, how common the word is and how often you looked it up. A long phrase shows its first lines: a tap opens it whole in place, ▲ closes it.
One dictionary at a time: ◀ ▶ or a swipe. Under it: related words, synonyms, expressions, forms, origin — › opens the whole list, with ◀ ▶ for its pages at the top.
AI tabs ask only when you tap them. With \"%1$s\" (AI → Modules) the others are ready when you open them. A module with nothing ticked has no tab and sends nothing.
No offline translation: Translate shows AI only, a phrase opens on word by word.
Not enough free space: %1$d MB needed, %2$d MB free.
Analysis (grammar, words) and Context (explanation, examples), as tabs inside; asked when you tap.
On some readers scrolling redraws the whole screen when it stops; by pages, a swipe up or down turns a whole page.
The English step in between, smaller, under the translation. Nothing is translated again.

Two tabs: Offline, translated on the device at once, and AI, asked when you tap it. The small print at the bottom says the text\'s language and how it was translated. With Show the English, the English step of a translation through English is under it, smaller.
Card → Appearance → Turning: Scroll, or Pages — a swipe up or down turns a whole page, and the line over the icons shows the pages, the open one thick.
Opens the selected text in this card; ← returns to the word before.
To another app: notes, Anki, a messenger.
The selected text in your web search.
Selects the whole line or article.
A tap beside the selection closes it and its menu.

Download packs… lists the pairs; a pack brings its dictionary, grammar and offline translation. A ticked pair is used by the card. ✕ removes a pair and what no other pair needs. Update the packs appears when the release has newer files.
Mozilla\'s models, through English: fast, any device, about 30 MB per direction. The meaning comes through; informal and formal you (du/Sie), gender and turns of phrase may get lost.
Straight between the languages, no English in between: closer to the original. About 170 MB per model, 4 GB of memory.
An AI model on the device (Tencent Hy-MT2, 1.1 GB): the most natural, but slow; needs 6 GB of memory and an int8-capable CPU.
The checkbox in the Fast · Mozilla method: the English step under a translation through English, smaller. Nothing is translated again for it.
AI → Modules: Translate, Analysis, Context, a box for each part; ✎ edits what a part asks. A module with no part ticked has no tab and sends nothing.

Only when you tap an AI tab, or a phrase opens on one (Card → Opening): the selected text and the answer language go to the provider you chose, with your key. Nothing else from the device. Answers are kept on the device.
Packs, models and other dictionaries are downloaded only when you ask: from the project\'s GitHub releases (models also from their original site) and the dictionary sources you pick.
This build asks GitHub for the latest release only when you press Check now (⚙ App → Updates): one request, nothing about you; never by itself.
☆ in the card saves a word as its base form (Häusern → Haus), a phrase as it is. A filled star: saved already.
Everything you open, the last 1,000, with how many times you looked each up; an entry keeps its AI answers, so it opens offline later. Card → Opening → History turns it off.
✕ removes one entry, Clear history the whole history; what is saved stays.
The TSV button saves the open list in Download/InkPeek: text, meaning, AI translation, language, date — Anki imports it as is.
Export saves everything (saved, history, AI answers) as one file in Download/InkPeek; Import adds from such a file what this device does not have.
A copy of everything is made each day in InkPeek/backup, the last five kept: to go back to one, Import it.
The language of menus and settings. The answers (dictionaries, translations, AI) follow it unless set in Languages → Translation.
Light, dark (white on black) or as Android\'s night mode; for the card and the settings.
InkPeek keeps its packs, Notes and copies in the InkPeek folder and reads other dictionaries\' folders (KOReader\'s too): it needs access to files.
InkPeek asks GitHub for a newer version only when you press Check now; it never checks by itself. Update downloads it, Android\'s installer asks you to confirm.
Languages you learn, two at most: their translation, dictionaries with their grammar, AI\'s analysis in them.
Two at most: untick one first
No pack %1$s yet: get it in Packs

Under Language of the answers, tick up to two languages you learn. A text already in the answer language then opens in them: a line under the title (ru → de, en); Dictionary — a language per page (◀ ▶), its pack\'s line and the translated words with their own grammar and frequency (a tap opens a word\'s card); Translate — the offline translation into each; AI — about those versions, explained in your language. Each answer language keeps its own list; nothing ticked: as before.
